page: Microsoft Azure E2ads_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the Eadsv7 family, powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at 4.5 GHz. This configuration features 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, supported by a 32 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with a 118 GB local disk, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. The virtualization layer is managed via Microsoft Hyper-V.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The instance achieves top-tier status in single-core metrics, including stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. However, due to its low core count, multi-core performance is weak, falling into the bottom performance tier for stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, PassMark CPU score, and PassMark database operations. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is average, while small-block read-only memory bandwidth is weak. Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput also rank in the lower tiers.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E2ads_v7 offers a high memory density relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high parallel processing power. Given its strong single-threaded performance but limited multi-core capacity, this server is best suited for lightweight databases, single-threaded processing tasks, caching layers with moderate throughput requirements, and general-purpose applications needing a larger memory footprint than standard compute-to-RAM ratios provide.
